title: Conflicts with lfm-moe-stream / inkling-stream in MLXBackend.load/loadLarge and ModelCatalog.Entry: an easy resolution undoes ModelStore
scenario: engine-ab replaces `#huggingFaceLoadModelContainer(...)` with `loadModelContainer(from: #hubDownloader(ModelStore.hub), ..., configuration: storeConfiguration(for:))` in `.llm`, and does the same in loadLarge. lfm-moe-stream and inkling-stream rewrite these same hunks: `case .llm where target.streamed == nil:` still calls `#huggingFaceLoadModelContainer`, and the non-streamed VLM path calls `#hubDownloader()`. If the conflict is resolved by taking their side, MLX and Inkling loads go back to HubCache.default (Library/Caches/huggingface/hub). That location is not migrated and iOS can purge it, the local-first check never sees those files, and the 10.3 GB Inkling DWQ is downloaded a second time while the old copy stays in Application Support. If it is resolved the other way, with storeConfiguration placed before the `target.streamed` branch, a streamed entry would load the full resident snapshot. Streamed entries share the repo LocallyInferred/Inkling-2-Mini-MLX-3.1bpw-DWQ with the resident DWQ tier, so ~9.6 GB would be resident and jetsam is certain at the ~5.3 GB limit. ModelCatalog.Entry also conflicts (engine/xybridSource vs streamed), and so do the `all` list region and .github/workflows/build.yml.
evidence: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/engine-ab origin/lfm-moe-stream` gives CONFLICT in MLXBackend.swift (merged lines 239-284, 316-368, 419-431), ModelCatalog.swift (Entry properties and the static list) and build.yml. inkling-stream conflicts in the same files. lfm-moe-stream diff: `case .llm where target.streamed == nil: return try await #huggingFaceLoadModelContainer(configuration: Self.configuration(for: target), ...)` and `loaded = try await VLMModelFactory.shared.loadContainer(from: #hubDownloader(), ...)`. engine-ab MLXBackend.swift lines 245 and 287 use `#hubDownloader(ModelStore.hub)` with `Self.storeConfiguration(for: target)`. Against integration, engine-ab conflicts only in docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md.
fix: When merging either stream branch after engine-ab, keep `#hubDownloader(ModelStore.hub)` plus `storeConfiguration(for:)` for every Hugging Face path, and remove all `#huggingFaceLoadModelContainer` and `#hubDownloader()` calls. Compute storeConfiguration only in the non-streamed branch, after the `if let build = target.streamed` check. Keep both Entry property blocks (engine, xybridSource, streamed). Afterwards, check that `git grep 'hubDownloader()\|huggingFaceLoadModelContainer' ios/AgentConsole` returns nothing.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim; the merge hazard checks out in git. Running `git merge-tree --write-tree` on origin/engine-ab with origin/lfm-moe-stream, and again with origin/inkling-stream, gives content conflicts in exactly the claimed files: MLXBackend.swift, ModelCatalog.swift, .github/workflows/build.yml and docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md. Against integration, engine-ab conflicts only in ENGINEERING-LOG.md.

In the conflicted MLXBackend.swift (merge tree 6c42a2b), the engine-ab side of `load()` and `loadLarge()` has the `wrongEngine` guard, `storeConfiguration(for:)`, `#hubDownloader(ModelStore.hub)` and `noteDownloaded`. The lfm-moe-stream side has `case .llm where target.streamed == nil:` calling `#huggingFaceLoadModelContainer(configuration: Self.configuration(for: target), ...)`, plus a non-streamed VLM path that uses `#hubDownloader()`.

If the conflict is resolved by taking the stream side, MLX and Inkling loads go back to the default HubCache under Library/Caches/huggingface/hub. engine-ab's ModelStore.swift moves snapshots out of that folder: it names it `legacyHubRoot` and keeps its own cache in Application Support/Models. Loads would then bypass the local-first check and download Inkling again.

The other failure mode also holds. In lfm-moe-stream's ModelCatalog.swift, the streamed Inkling entries (lines 129 and 132) use repo "LocallyInferred/Inkling-2-Mini-MLX-3.1bpw-DWQ", the same repo as the resident DWQ entry (10.3 GB download, residentGB 9.60). `storeConfiguration` checks only the repo snapshot. So if a resolution uses it before or instead of the `target.streamed` branch, a streamed entry would load the full resident model, which is far over the ~5.3 GB limit.

The ModelCatalog.Entry conflict is confirmed by merge-tree. Medium severity fits: this is a merge hazard, not a defect on any single branch.

UPHELD(medium): I confirmed the core of the claim but not every detail. Running `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/engine-ab origin/{lfm-moe-stream,inkling-stream}` gives content conflicts in ios/AgentConsole/Inference/MLXBackend.swift, ModelCatalog.swift, .github/workflows/build.yml and docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md for both stream branches.

On engine-ab, the `.llm` case at MLXBackend.swift:243-249 and loadLarge at about line 287 use `Self.storeConfiguration(for:)`, `#hubDownloader(ModelStore.hub)` and `ModelStore.noteDownloaded`. storeConfiguration is at line 82; it swaps in `.directory(localSnapshot)` when a local snapshot exists. lfm-moe-stream rewrites the same hunks. At line 120 it has `case .llm where target.streamed == nil: #huggingFaceLoadModelContainer(configuration: Self.configuration(for:))`, and at line 171 the non-streamed loadLarge path uses `#hubDownloader()` with the plain configuration. inkling-stream has the same pattern at lines 115 and 165. So if the conflict is resolved by taking the stream side, the ModelStore and local-first behaviour is silently lost on those paths: both fall back to the default hub cache. The resolution is also fiddly in another way. The loadLarge signatures differ: engine-ab has `epoch:` and the stream branches do not. Mixing the two sides can therefore also fail to compile.

One sub-point is overstated. If storeConfiguration is merely computed before the `target.streamed` branch, nothing extra becomes resident, because the streamed path loads from StreamedModelStore's directory and ignores that configuration. The real memory hazard is different. Suppose the resolver keeps engine-ab's unguarded `case .llm:`, which drops `where target.streamed == nil`. That case comes before `case .llm, .vlm`, so a streamed LLM entry (such as the streamed LFM tiers) would go down the full hub snapshot path instead of the streaming path.

I did not verify the claims about the HubCache.default location, iOS purging it, or the 10.3 GB re-download. They are plausible consequences but were not checked. Overall this is a real, evidenced merge hazard, and medium severity is reasonable.

title: Fleet bench with no modelId and a Xybrid model selected hands a Xybrid entry to the MLX BenchmarkRunner
scenario: The user picks a Xybrid entry in Settings, for example xybrid-lfm2.5-8b-a1b-q4_0. A fleet `bench` task then arrives without model_id. The new engine guard (`e.engine == .mlx`) covers only an explicit id. The fallback `entry = ModelCatalog.selected` passes the Xybrid entry to `BenchmarkRunner(backend: mlx).run`. beginBenchmark serves it, and MLXBackend.performLoad throws `BackendError.wrongEngine`, after the 10 s settle and after a jetsam breadcrumb is written. The fleet receives a 'failed' receipt labelled engine 'mlx' for a GGUF model, not a clear rejection.
evidence: NodeService.swift:499-505: `guard let e = ModelCatalog.entry(id: id), e.engine == .mlx else { throw ... }` ... `} else { entry = ModelCatalog.selected }`. MLXBackend.swift:238: `guard target.engine == .mlx else { throw BackendError.wrongEngine(target.displayName) }`. BenchmarkRunner sets `receipt.engine = "mlx"` unconditionally.
fix: After choosing the entry, add `guard entry.engine == .mlx else { throw BenchError.unknownModel(entry.id, known: ModelCatalog.all.map(\.id)) }`. Alternatively, fall back to `ModelCatalog.defaultEntry` when the selection is a Xybrid entry.
notes: UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim; the code on origin/engine-ab confirms it. In NodeService.swift:498-506, the `e.engine == .mlx` guard runs only in the `if let id = p.modelId` branch. When model_id is missing, the code falls back to `entry = ModelCatalog.selected`. ModelCatalog.swift:182-186 resolves `selected` from `available`, which is `pickerEntries` filtered to what this device supports, and `pickerEntries` is `all + xybridEntries` (line 169). So a persisted selection such as xybrid-lfm2.5-8b-a1b-q4_0 is returned as is. That entry then reaches `BenchmarkRunner(backend: mlx).run`. That function calls `backend.beginBenchmark(entry)`, sets `receipt.engine = "mlx"` unconditionally (BenchmarkRunner.swift:65), waits through the 10 s settle loop, and writes `JetsamBreadcrumb.set(... engine: "mlx" ...)` (line 138). After that, `loadBenchmarkModel` reaches MLXBackend.swift:238, `guard target.engine == .mlx else { throw BackendError.wrongEngine }`. The fleet therefore gets a "failed" receipt labelled mlx, not a clear up-front rejection. One caveat: the MemoryBudget or available-memory checks could return "skipped" before the load for some Xybrid entries. That outcome is equally misleading, so it does not refute the defect. Severity low (wrong or confusing result plus about 10 s wasted, no crash). Fix: after choosing the entry, add `guard entry.engine == .mlx else { throw BenchError.unknownModel(entry.id, known: ModelCatalog.all.map(\.id)) }`, or fall back to `ModelCatalog.defaultEntry` when the selected entry is a Xybrid one.

UPHELD(high): I tried to refute this and could not; the defect is real on origin/engine-ab.

How it happens:
- In NodeService.swift (lines 499-506), the `e.engine == .mlx` guard runs only when `p.modelId` is set. Otherwise `entry = ModelCatalog.selected`.
- In ModelCatalog.swift, `selected` returns the first `available` entry matching the stored id (lines 182-188). `available` is `pickerEntries.filter(\.isSupportedOnThisDevice)` (line 173), and `pickerEntries` is `all + xybridEntries` (line 169). A Xybrid selection such as xybrid-lfm2.5-8b-a1b-q4_0 (line 162) is therefore returned as is.
- That entry goes to `BenchmarkRunner(backend: mlx).run`. Nothing in `run` or `measure` checks the engine.
- `measure` sets `receipt.engine = "mlx"` unconditionally (BenchmarkRunner.swift:65), runs the 10 s settle (lines 98-103) and writes the jetsam breadcrumb with engine "mlx" (lines 137-140). Only then does MLXBackend's load path throw `BackendError.wrongEngine` (MLXBackend.swift:238).

Nothing crashes on the way: `MLXBackend.configuration(for:)` falls through to `ModelConfiguration(id: entry.repo)`.

One small correction to the scenario: depending on the entry's size, the `MemoryBudget.fit` or headroom checks (lines 121-136) may record "skipped" before the load instead of "failed". Either way the fleet gets an MLX-labelled receipt for a GGUF/Xybrid model, not a clear rejection.

Severity low is right, since nothing is corrupted. The proposed fix works: after choosing the entry, add `guard entry.engine == .mlx else { throw BenchError.unknownModel(...) }`, or fall back to `ModelCatalog.defaultEntry`.

title: localSnapshot treats a snapshot as complete without tokenizer_config.json or chat_template.jinja, and never re-downloads
scenario: requiredFiles needs only config.json, one of tokenizer.json or tokenizer_config.json, and the weight shards. The downloader fetches modelDownloadPatterns = ["*.safetensors", "*.json", "*.jinja"] with up to 8 concurrent files. A snapshot can therefore have every shard and tokenizer.json while missing tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja or generation_config.json, for example after an interrupted download or a migrated legacy snapshot. Such a snapshot is reported complete and loaded through `.directory(snapshot)` with no network call. The tokenizer then either fails to load or runs without the chat template, giving wrong output or tool-call format inference. Every later load takes the same local path, so the file is never fetched again until the user deletes the model.
evidence: ModelStore.swift:156-177: `guard exists("config.json") ...; if exists("tokenizer.json") { files.append("tokenizer.json") } else if exists("tokenizer_config.json") ... else { return nil }`. Nothing else is required. MLXBackend.storeConfiguration switches to `.directory(snapshot)` whenever localSnapshot is non-nil. Vendored ModelFactory.swift:7-8: `tokenizerDownloadPatterns = ["*.json", "*.jinja"]` and `modelDownloadPatterns = ["*.safetensors"] + tokenizerDownloadPatterns`.
fix: Require tokenizer_config.json whenever tokenizer.json exists. Also record the full file list from the snapshot at `noteDownloaded` time, after a network load has finished, and require all recorded files in localSnapshot. When a load from `.directory` fails, fall back once to the network configuration instead of failing permanently.
notes:
UPHELD(medium): The code does what the claim says. In origin/engine-ab:ios/AgentConsole/Inference/ModelStore.swift, requiredFiles (about lines 156-177) requires only config.json, one of tokenizer.json or tokenizer_config.json, and the weight shards. localSnapshot treats any snapshot that passes those checks and the size checks as complete, and the first time it sees one it records a manifest of only those files. MLXBackend.storeConfiguration (line 85) and MemoryEmbedder (line 52) then switch to `.directory(snapshot)` with no network call. noteDownloaded records only the same requiredFiles list. There is no fallback to the network when a load from `.directory` fails, so a partial snapshot stays partial until the user deletes the model.

An interrupted download can plausibly leave this state, and the library source makes it more likely, not less. In swift-huggingface (HubClient+Files.swift, about lines 2052-2085), the Xet trait is not enabled in this app, so snapshotTransport returns .lfs for every file. All files go through one queue of up to 8 concurrent downloads, sorted by size from largest to smallest. The shards and tokenizer.json therefore finish first, and the small tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja and generation_config.json come last. If the app is killed or the network drops in that last stretch, the snapshot already has refs/main, config.json, tokenizer.json and every shard, but is missing the files that carry the chat template and the EOS settings.

The window is narrow: config.json is also small, so it lands in the same last batch, and a missing generation_config.json is probably the most likely result. Even so, the defect is real and persistent, and the low severity is appropriate.

The fix is to require tokenizer_config.json whenever tokenizer.json exists, and to require chat_template.jinja and generation_config.json when the repo listing includes them. Recording the full list of files in the snapshot at noteDownloaded time also covers this, as does falling back once to the network configuration when a `.directory` load fails.

UPHELD(medium): I confirmed the defect at low severity. On origin/engine-ab, ModelStore.requiredFiles (around lines 156-177) requires only config.json, one of tokenizer.json or tokenizer_config.json, and the weight shards. localSnapshot returns the snapshot once those exist with sizes above zero. On first sight it records a manifest of only those files, and it never checks tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja or generation_config.json. MLXBackend.storeConfiguration (lines 82-90) switches to `.directory(snapshot)` whenever localSnapshot is non-nil. noteDownloaded runs only after a successful network load. No code path falls back to the network when a directory load fails, so a snapshot with files missing stays broken until the user deletes it.

The missing-file state can happen. In swift-huggingface (HubClient+Files.swift, about lines 2040-2090), downloadSnapshot without XET sends every file through the LFS work list. It sorts that list by size, largest first, and runs up to 8 downloads at once in a throwing task group. The small files (tokenizer_config.json, chat_template.jinja, config.json, generation_config.json) therefore download last and close together. If one of them fails or is cancelled while config.json has already finished, the shards, tokenizer.json and config.json are all present but tokenizer_config.json or chat_template.jinja is not. localSnapshot then calls that snapshot complete on every later load.

The window is narrow: it needs an interruption or failure in the last few small-file downloads, or a migrated legacy snapshot that is missing files. That keeps this low severity, but it is a reachable runtime bug and not a theoretical one. I did not trace exactly what the vendored swift-transformers tokenizer loader does without tokenizer_config.json, whether it throws or runs without a chat template. Either result is wrong behaviour that persists. The proposed fix is sound: require tokenizer_config.json and any recorded *.jinja files, and fall back once to the network configuration when a directory load fails.

title: docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md conflicts with current integration
scenario: Merging engine-ab into origin/integration (HEAD b58fc6b) stops on a content conflict in the engineering log, because both sides appended entries. No Swift file conflicts with integration.
evidence: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/integration origin/engine-ab` gives `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md` and nothing else.
fix: Resolve by keeping both appended sections in chronological order.
notes: UPHELD(high): I confirmed the claim. After fetching, origin/integration is at b58fc6b and origin/engine-ab is at 1e548fd. Running `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/integration origin/engine-ab` exits with code 1. Its only output is `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md`, and no other path conflicts, so no Swift file conflicts. This is a low-severity merge hazard limited to the docs log. The fix is to keep both appended sections in chronological order.

UPHELD(high): I reproduced the claim. After `git fetch`, origin/integration is at b58fc6b and origin/engine-ab is at 1e548fd. Running `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/integration origin/engine-ab` exits with code 1 and lists docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md at stages 1, 2 and 3, with "CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md". No other file conflicts, so no Swift file is involved. It is a real merge hazard, and the fix is simple: keep both appended sections in date order. Low severity is right.
